messages:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — private rollout for acme-corp canary is stuck. Control plane shows config pushed (seq=457) but most agents in the VPC are still on seq=454. Canary split is 1% and traffic is inconsistent across zones. Anyone seen this pattern in air-gapped customers?
Liam Chen: Hmm. Do you have the agent logs or our push audit?
Maya Patel: Pasted a snippet from control-plane audit: 
```
INFO 2026-02-12T09:12:03Z rollout=457 push=ok
WARN 2026-02-12T09:14:20Z agent=10.4.12.7 ack_seq=454 expected=457
WARN 2026-02-12T09:15:41Z agent=10.4.22.9 ack_seq=454 expected=457
```
Maya Patel: Control plane sent the delta bundle but agent heartbeats show no ack. This is happening only in VPC/on-prem rollouts (air-gapped).
Elena Rodriguez: For air-gapped flows we rely on agent-initiated pulls. If their pull interval is long or network policy blocks egress, that'd explain it. What's our current ack_timeout for canaries?
Dan Kim: Default ack_timeout for private rollouts is 30m, canary window 10m. Guard rule: abort if error_rate increases >5% OR p95_latency +100ms vs baseline. But that's evaluated server-side; if agents haven't applied the config we get a split-brain — control plane thinks rollout active, agents still route old variant.
Maya Patel: Right. So apps end up with mixed routing and our canary metrics are meaningless. We need a reconciliation mechanism and better UX to surface unreconciled hosts.
Liam Chen: Agreed. I don't want a "force-commit" that bypasses on-host validation because that can hide real failures. Instead, we should make rollout progress depend on agent ACKs and fail-open to fallback variant if a host hasn't applied canary after ack_timeout.
Elena Rodriguez: Fallback helps, but we also need to surface which hosts are stale. Console should show per-VPC table: pending_hosts, last_ack_ts, host_seq, and provide actions (pause/requeue/bundle upload).
Dan Kim: Also discuss internal API: control plane currently pushes via websocket for hosted customers. Air-gapped customers use agent pull + artifact bundle stored in our blob service. Some customers disallow outbound to our blob endpoint, so operators upload artifact bundles manually. We should support an "ops-upload" reconciliation path.
Maya Patel: Proposed rollout config snippet (for discussion):
```
{
  "rollout_id": 457,
  "canary_split": "1%",
  "require_agent_ack": true,
  "ack_timeout": "10m",
  "max_failed_hosts": 1,
  "fallback_policy": "serve-stable-variant"
}
```
Maya Patel: With require_agent_ack=true, control plane will mark hosts as PENDING until ack. Only when pct_acked >= threshold do we shift the split.
Liam Chen: Nice. We must be careful with ack_timeout defaults — 10m is aggressive for some on-prem sites with flaky management network. Maybe make it per-tenant override and the console suggests a recommended value based on historical ack latencies.
Elena Rodriguez: Another idea: soft-fallback routing at the edge — if host hasn't applied canary, route that host's traffic to a local fallback variant so end-users get consistent behavior while rollout finishes. But that complicates KV cache and session affinity.
Dan Kim: On the control-plane side, we should add a sequence reconciliation endpoint: agents report their last_applied_seq and control-plane returns missing delta(s). For air-gapped ops-upload, ops runner can call our admin endpoint to mark a bundle delivered to the customer and trigger a requeue.
SRE Bot: alert: rollout_delay acme-corp 2h (auto-generated).
Liam Chen: For telemetry: emit events rollout.apply_attempt, rollout.apply_success, rollout.apply_fail with fields [tenant, host, seq, duration_ms, error_codes]. Create a dashboard: ack-duration histogram + heatmap by VPC. Alert if pct_acked < 80% after ack_timeout.
Maya Patel: UX changes in console I want to spike: - per-rollout progress bar based on pct_acked - table of unreconciled hosts with last_ack_ts - buttons: Pause, Requeue Bundle, Force-Abort (danger) - show why a host failed to ack (e.g., network, disk full, agent crash).
Elena Rodriguez: Also add an explicit "stuck" state: if rollout state == PENDING and no progress for X, auto-pause and create a ticket suggestion with diagnostics bundle link.
Dan Kim: Internal API debate: do we maintain a push-only model for hosted and a pull-only model for private, or unify with an "orchestrator" abstraction (push where possible, otherwise fallback to pull or ops-upload)? I vote for unified abstraction so rollouts code path converges.
Liam Chen: Agreed on abstraction. Implementation plan: 1) add agent ack field + reconciliation endpoint (spike) 2) telemetry + dashboard 3) console UX for pending hosts 4) ops-upload workflow and manual requeue 5) default ack_timeout tweak and per-tenant overrides.
Maya Patel: I'll do a small spike for (1) and (2) — create an internal RFC with API shape. Dan, can you take console mockups for (3)?
Dan Kim: Yep, I'll mockup a per-rollout panel and a pending-hosts widget.
Maya Patel: Thanks — assigning self+Dan. Will share RFC in #eng-platform once spike results are in.
Elena Rodriguez: One last note: change our canary evaluation to compare only hosts that have acked the new seq to avoid noisy metrics. That will make early-stage canary metrics reliable.
Liam Chen: +1. Also emit a metric rollout.ack_lag_seconds to help recommend ack_timeout.
Maya Patel: ok, closing for now. Will post RFC link. :thumbsup:
SRE Bot: Reaction :white_check_mark: to Maya Patel's message.
deploy-bot: deploy 20260212-canary-checkpoint started for rollout 457.
Maya Patel: thanks — I'll follow up with logs and the RFC.
